- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for such periods.
- Model overestimates prices in early forecast horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for first 7 days.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent 7-day low.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% per day for 3–5 days post-shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period price surges (last 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive and price has been rising for 3+ days.
